method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase. Not independent or human review.
scope: Complete relations chapter OLP-0011–OLP-0019, 104 content-bearing aligned blocks; diagram-only whitespace not counted as translated prose.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A binary relation on A is any subset of A squared, including the empty and universal relations. Ordered coordinate positions matter.
samples.checks: No requirement of a natural relation; universal and existential language preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Equally useful reversed pair encodings undermine an arbitrary ontological identification; treating a relation as a set is not discovery of metaphysical identity.
samples.checks: Philosophical objection is presented as source argument, not an added theorem. Benacerraf citation and both conditional branches/footnote retained in editable source.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If membership were merely another name of a set, the expression would become a list of names rather than a proposition.
samples.checks: Predicate versus singular term preserved; nonsense example translated as a list without inserting a verb that would make a proposition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Anti-symmetric relations permit both directions only for equal elements, and need not contain self-pairs. Asymmetric relations permit no two-way pair at all.
samples.checks: Distinct from merely not symmetric; empty-domain qualification and non-reflexive/non-irreflexive cases preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: R-related points have equal classes via symmetry and transitivity; equal classes imply Rxy using reflexivity at y.
samples.checks: Both directions and each property use retained. Exactly n residue classes for positive n; natural number zero convention unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Adding all diagonal pairs to a strict order yields a partial order; removing them from a partial order yields a strict order.
samples.checks: Transitivity proof separates both-pairs-in-R from equality cases. Connectedness yields the linear variant. Divisibility on integers is not anti-symmetric because 1 and -1 divide each other.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A graph specifies both its vertex set and edge relation. An isolated vertex changes the graph without changing the edge set.
samples.checks: Four-vertex versus three-vertex diagrams, loop and edge directions preserved. Restored source explanation of plural vertex in Marathi.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A tree node need have at most one immediate predecessor, not necessarily exactly one. A branch is maximal, and finite branching does not imply finitely many vertices.
samples.checks: Least versus merely minimal, immediate predecessor versus ancestor, infinite-branch claim and weak Konig scope preserved. Source notation defects separated into SOURCE_ISSUES-B002.json.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Relative product follows R then S through an existential intermediate point. Restriction requires both coordinates in A; application only constrains the input. Transitive closure uses positive path length.
samples.checks: No inverse-coordinate or composition-order reversal; reflexive closure separately adds identity.

corrections_before_release: Restored explicit repeated L and G symbols in relation example to preserve formula multiplicities.
Improved plural formula grammar in the tree introduction.
legitimate_exceptions: K\H{o}nig is preserved as a proper name and source accent macro.
TikZ keys, identifiers, source comments, file paths, bibliography titles and mathematical symbols remain unchanged.
External cumulative-set and real-line conditional branches remain in editable translation; chapter reader takes the original false branch.
limitations: Some advanced Marathi compounds are explicitly provisional; no specialist fluency certification.
All nine source units translated, but final corpus has 706 units remaining after the cumulative 16-unit tranche.
Source defects are not silently repaired; separate editorial notes explain them.
